title: QR Code (GS1 + generic)
objectives: Understand QR via a real-life analogy
Encode GS1 element strings + Digital Link URLs into QR
Design QR for consumer scanning success

sections.markdown:
**Think of QR as the consumer's poster child of 2D barcodes.**

Invented by Denso Wave in 1994 for automotive parts — now the most recognizable code type on Earth. Every phone camera has a native QR reader. Iconic finder patterns + high capacity + configurable error correction.

- **Consumer familiarity** — no learning curve; users know 'scan this square.'
- **Very high capacity** — 4 KB with the smallest correction level.
- **Error correction 4 levels** — L (7%), M (15%), Q (25%), H (30%). Higher = more redundancy = bigger code but tolerates more damage.
- **Structure** — finder patterns (3 corners), timing pattern, alignment patterns, data + ECC.
- **GS1 mode** — QR can encode GS1 element strings with FNC1 marker; supported but less used than plain URL QR.
- **Digital Link fits QR beautifully** — consumer-facing packaging with `https://id.gs1.org/…` URLs.

**Why every consumer-facing Flutter app scans + generates QR:** payments (UPI in India, Alipay/WeChat in China), Wi-Fi credentials, business cards, event tickets, marketing campaigns, deep links. **The QR tax** — because they're so universal, they're also the #1 phishing vector: attackers stick fake QRs over real ones on parking meters, restaurant tables, ATMs. Displaying the destination URL BEFORE opening is essential.

**QR (Quick Response) code** is a 2D matrix symbology invented by Denso Wave. Models 1 (original) + Model 2 (current standard). Configurable Reed-Solomon error correction (L/M/Q/H). Capacity: up to ~2953 bytes at L level (Version 40). Encodable data: numeric, alphanumeric, binary, kanji, plus a special GS1 mode for element strings. Standardized as ISO/IEC 18004. Free to use — Denso Wave holds the patent but doesn't enforce it commercially.

## Generate + scan QR in Flutter
## Common mistakes
**Mistake 1: L-level EC on printed packaging.** Rain / scratches degrade past 7 %; use M or Q.
**Mistake 2: Logo overlay without H-level EC.** Center logo eats correction budget; require H if you want a logo.
**Mistake 3: Auto-opening URLs.** Attackers stick fake QRs on parking meters. Show destination first.
**Mistake 4: Storing tokens in URL.** QR is publicly scannable; anyone who photographs the code can replay.
**Mistake 5: Too small print.** Below ~1.5 cm for consumer scan → focus issues on low-end phones.
**Mistake 6: Poor contrast.** White-on-dark backgrounds sometimes scan; test on real devices.
**Mistake 7: Version too high without need.** Big QR = harder to scan; use the smallest version that fits your data + ECC choice.
**Mistake 8: Not testing on old Android + iPhone SE.** Older cameras autofocus slower; small codes fail.
## Best practices
**1. Show destination URL** before opening; block obvious phishing patterns.
**2. M-level EC for indoor printing;** Q for outdoor; H for logo overlay.
**3. Minimum 2 cm quiet-zone-included size** for consumer scan.
**4. Contrast ratio 4:1 minimum** — dark modules on light background.
**5. HTTPS-only URLs in production QR.**
**6. Version-track the URL** — allows regeneration + tracking.
**7. Analytics on scan** — count campaign scans via unique URL parameters.
**8. Consider Micro QR** for very-small codes; supported on modern scanners.
## Practice programs
**Practice 1 (Easy)** — Generate a URL QR + display it.
**Practice 2 (Easy)** — Scan a QR + route by prefix (upi:// / WIFI: / https://).
**Practice 3 (Medium)** — Logo-overlaid QR with H-level EC; test scan rate.
**Practice 4 (Medium)** — Consumer scan with destination-confirmation dialog.
**Practice 5 (Hard)** — GS1 Digital Link QR generation with proper AI encoding.
**Practice 6 (Expert)** — Phishing-defense scanner: flag suspicious URLs against a threat-intel list before opening.
## Interview Q&A

**Q1: How do you pick an error-correction level?**

**A:** **L (7 %)** — clean digital displays; smallest code; use when the medium is highly reliable. **M (15 %)** — default for printed packaging + business cards + Wi-Fi codes; balances size + robustness. **Q (25 %)** — outdoor posters, weathered surfaces, delivery labels. **H (30 %)** — necessary when you want to overlay a logo in the center; the redundancy compensates for lost modules. **Trade-offs:** higher EC = MORE modules = physically LARGER code = potentially harder scan at distance. So pick the LOWEST EC that meets your damage tolerance. **Rule:** consumer-facing marketing QR = M; outdoor billboard = Q; logo-overlaid = H; test in worst-case conditions.

**Q2: What's the phishing risk with QR + how do you mitigate?**

**A:** **Risk:** attackers replace a legitimate QR (parking meter, restaurant menu, ATM cash slip) with a sticker QR pointing to phishing / malware URL. User scans, phone auto-opens URL, credentials stolen. **Real incidents:** parking-meter QR scams have taken millions in India + US. **Defense in the app:** (1) show the DESTINATION URL BEFORE opening — a preview banner or confirmation dialog. (2) Compare against a threat-intel list (Google Safe Browsing, custom malicious-domain list). (3) Warn on IDN homograph domains (`ăpple.com`). (4) Detect URL shorteners (`bit.ly`, `t.co`) that hide destination + expand server-side first. (5) HTTPS-only for known sensitive contexts (payments, banking). (6) Sandbox opening — some apps show a WebView preview before the full browser. (7) User-education UX. **This is now table-stakes for any consumer QR-scanning Flutter app.**

**Q3: How do QR + DataMatrix differ + when do you pick each?**

**A:** **QR wins when:** (1) Consumer scan (native camera support everywhere); (2) Higher capacity (~4 KB vs ~2 KB); (3) Configurable error correction; (4) Consumer familiarity + trust; (5) Marketing + campaigns + payments. **DataMatrix wins when:** (1) Small print size (3 × 3 mm feasible); (2) Regulated pharma + medical + industrial; (3) Fixed high error correction; (4) DPM (Direct Part Marking on metal); (5) Established installed base of specialty scanners. **Rule:** consumer → QR; industrial + regulated → DataMatrix. **Sunrise 2027** blurs this — GS1 encourages 2D on all retail packaging; brands pick QR (consumer-friendly) or DataMatrix (small print) based on package size. Interviewer signal: knowing both are ISO-standardized + specific use-case fit.

**Q4: How do you handle UPI payment QR codes in a Flutter app?**

**A:** UPI QRs use the `upi://pay?...` scheme (not `https://`). Params include `pa` (payee address), `pn` (name), `am` (amount), `cu` (currency), `tn` (transaction note). **Scan flow:** (1) Detect `upi://` prefix. (2) Parse query params. (3) Show confirmation UI: 'Pay ₹100 to Merchant@bank?' (4) `launchUrl(Uri.parse(upiUri), mode: LaunchMode.externalApplication)` opens the user's UPI app (GPay, PhonePe, Paytm). (5) UPI app handles the actual payment + returns result via callback. **Safety:** always confirm amount + payee before launch; never auto-execute. **Compliance:** RBI + NPCI guidelines govern UPI QRs; static vs dynamic; merchant registration. **Merchant side:** Flutter apps can generate static QRs bound to a UPI address + optional amount; scan-and-pay flows for street vendors + kiranas. Interviewer bonus: India-specific familiarity.

**Q5: What's the story with Micro QR + rQR?**

**A:** **Micro QR** — smaller variant with 4 versions (M1-M4); one finder pattern instead of three; capacity 5-35 numeric characters. Fits where regular QR is too big (mini stickers, embedded metal parts). Supported by most modern scanners but rare in consumer wild. **rQR (Rectangular Micro QR, 2022)** — rectangular Micro QR; fits narrow strips of space (product bottoms, cable labels). Newer + less-supported. **When to use:** rare in mainstream Flutter apps; niche in labeling / industrial. Encourage regular QR for anything consumer-facing. Interviewer bonus: knowing they exist AT ALL + when.

**Q6: How would you build a QR scan-and-pay app with phishing defense?**

**A:** **(1)** Camera scan via `mobile_scanner` restricted to QR format. **(2)** On detect, PARSE the URI + classify: `upi://` (UPI intent), `https://` (URL — potentially phishing), `WIFI:`, GS1 Digital Link, etc. **(3)** Route to type-specific UI. **(4)** URL flow: display destination hostname prominently ('You're about to open MYBANK.COM'); highlight punycode / IDN + suspicious TLDs. **(5)** Check against known-bad-domain feed (updated via Remote Config). **(6)** For UPI, parse + confirm amount + payee; show masking on payee ID. **(7)** For sensitive payloads, redirect to WebView with SSL cert + address bar visible. **(8)** Log all scans (pseudo-anonymized) for anti-abuse analysis. **(9)** Rate-limit scans in short intervals (fraud pattern). **(10)** Accessibility — voice out the destination for low-vision users. **This layered defense is the standard for consumer payment apps in India post-2023.**

## Real-world usage

- **UPI payments** — merchant QR at every shop in India.
- **Wi-Fi sharing** — home + restaurant hotspots.
- **Deep links** — app install + campaigns.
- **Business cards** — vCard QR.
- **Ticketing** — concert / airline / rail.
- **GS1 Digital Link** — Sunrise 2027 retail migration.
- **NOT ideal for** — very small print (DataMatrix); regulated pharma (DataMatrix).

## Advanced notes

- **Versions 1-40** — module sizes 21×21 up to 177×177.
- **Encoding modes** — numeric (10 bits/3 digits), alphanumeric (11 bits/2 chars), byte (8 bits/char), kanji (13 bits/char).
- **Mask patterns** — 8 masks chosen automatically to maximize scannability.
- **Structured Append** — split a big payload across up to 16 QRs; rare.
- **Model 1 vs Model 2** — Model 2 (current) has alignment patterns.
- **Frame QR (Denso)** — decorated variant; less standard.
- **iQR** — Denso extension with more sizes + rectangular options.
- **QR + AR** — some AR apps use QR as anchor markers.
- **QR + payments** — EMVCo Merchant-Presented QR spec globally; UPI in India.
- **Print testing** — verify at real print size + on target scanners.
- **Dark/light theme mismatch** — some designers use dark modules on dark background; scanner fails.
- **QR generation service** — server-side rendering (Sharp, canvas) + delivery via CDN URL for dynamic marketing QRs.
